In Fujian, authorities estimate that almost 600,000 people were evacuated from high-risk, flood-prone areas. A further 128,000 people in 53 counties were also affected across Jiangxi, with emergency evacuations affecting 9,000 people.

Flooding, landslips and infrastructure damage were reported widely in the region. More than 2,500 teachers and students were trapped in a school compound in the Zhejiang city of Wenzhou on Wednesday after extreme rainfall caused flash floods in low-lying areas. At least 1,260 people reportedly had to be rescued in Putian after a river embankment collapsed on Thursday, flattening 100 homes. On Saturday, a landslip in a village of Suichuan county, in Jiangxi province, killed three people and nine others remaining missing.

events.title: ‘I fear the price could be high’: Inside the German state where the far-right surged
events.summary:
After the AfD’s landslide win in Saxony-Anhalt, people in the state capital share what they make of the result – and what comes next

• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Asking residents in a city where a seismic political event has just taken place ‘How do you feel?’ demands chutzpah – this struck me as I walked around Magdeburg, Germany on Monday. The night before, the far-right populist, anti-immigrant, pro-Kremlin party Alternative für Deustchland (AfD) had landslide 44% win in Saxony-Anhalt’s state elections, sending shock waves to Berlin, across Germany and way beyond. Regardless of how people in the capital voted, it felt like a bit of an affront to probe. Given the radical plans of the victors, a party classified by domestic intelligence as “rightwing extremist”, that is what I wanted to know. But from the 21-year-old Guinean-German paramedic I met at the central bus station, collecting donations for a local hospice, to the elderly couple returning to their apartment after a stroll down the Elbe river, almost everyone I met opened up to me warmly.

Judith, 88, was initially reluctant to talk, but shared some of her life story. Her experience as an eight-year-old refugee, forced to leave Poland in 1946 and eventually ending up move with her family in Magdeburg, had shaped her outlook on life, her successful career as a project engineer – as well as her politics. The news that AfD had not only won the election, but by such a wide margin, was “heartbreaking”, she said.

events.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?

events.title: Berlin: BER Airport Terminal 1 reopened after security scare

events.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
events.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

events.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
events.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

events.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus
events.summary: Nicole Anyomi has joined Alexia Putellas and other star names in signing for the ambitious English club London City Lionesses. The Germany winger told DW England is a better place to develop her game than back home.

events.title: Ukraine: Russia threatens 'devastating' Baltic response

events.summary: The death of Ratko Mladic did not close a dark chapter of European history; it reopened old wounds. The ideology that created him lives on. The Dayton peace agreement ended the war, not the divisions that produced it.

events.title: Norway's new King Haakon VIII takes oath in parliament
events.summary: The new king swore to uphold the constitution in parliament in Oslo, the first major institutional step of his reign. Haakon VIII's wife Queen Mette-Marit had to skip the event in the aftermath of her lung transplant.

events.title: US irks Germany, Europe with Russian G20 invite, press bans
events.summary: Russia's finance minister is at the G20 meeting in Asheville but some key US press corps members are not. The mood was already tense amid the lengthy Iran war and Trump's renewed beef with neighbor Canada.

events.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?

events.title: At Venice Film Festival, politics take center stage

events.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides, but it could backfire

events.title: Reports: UEFA backs off FIFA boycott threat

events.summary: As Gamescom 2026 opens in Cologne, AI, hardware costs and slowing user growth are putting pressure on the global games industry despite its current strength.

events.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
events.summary: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

events.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
events.summary: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.

events.title: Can we go green without forever chemicals?
events.summary: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?

events.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
events.summary: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

events.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
events.summary: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

events.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
events.summary: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

events.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
events.summary: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

events.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
events.summary: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

events.title: How a French Foreign Legion soldier dramatically escaped Colombian captors
events.summary: A French Foreign Legion soldier kidnapped by Colombian guerrillas escaped after nearly a month in captivity by overpowering a guard, jumping into a river with his hands tied and trekking for four days through the Andes to reach safety, according to a Colombian military source.

events.title: Kenya's crackdown on foreign workers raises concern among Burundians
events.summary: Some 16,000 Burundian refugees and asylum seekers live in Kenya, and many of them make a living through informal jobs – as carpenters, motorcycle taxi drivers, or clothing vendors. But since Monday, many have been afraid to go to work, and are now looking to leave the country. The reason: remarks made by Kenya’s president, which have sparked deep concern within the Burundian community. More from our correspondent Bastien Renouil.

events.title: Céline Dion's return to France: A French love affair
events.summary: Céline Dion’s hotly anticipated return to the stage is scheduled for this Saturday in Paris – the first of more than 16 concerts in the French capital in September and October. The shows mark a major milestone for 58-year-old Dion after years away from touring due to a rare neurological disorder. FRANCE 24's Aurore Cloé Dupuis tells us more.

events.title: Macron summit seeks boost for European space despite no-shows
events.summary: France is pressing ahead with a space summit shunned by the US tech giants and hampered by a lower-than-expected turnout from European leaders as President Emmanuel Macron seeks a stronger role for Europe in the competitive maelstrom of space. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley tells us more.

events.title: NY failed to disclose what it knew on 'toxic air' after 9/11
events.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Tuesday the release of tens of thousands of documents showing the city did not disclose all it knew about air toxicity after 9/11. The release comes ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, attacks that killed 2,977 people in the United States, mostly in the collapse of the Twin Towers in New York. In the years since, more than 9,400 have died from illnesses linked to their exposure to the area, according to a federal medical monitoring program.

events.title: Peru: 38 skeletons unearthed in ancient tomb
events.summary: Archaeologists in Peru have discovered a near-intact pre-Incan tomb, containing the skeletons of 38 individuals, along with gold and copper objects. The remains include those of an elite member of the Chimu civilization, which flourished between 900 and 1470 AD.

events.title: France's far-right National Rally fires policeman from security team over racist, sexist comments
events.summary: France's far-right National Rally (RN) has expelled a policeman from its ranks after bodycam footage of him making racist, homophobic and sexist remarks was published on Wednesday. The controversy threatens to revive scrutiny of the party's efforts to distance itself from its extremist past ahead of next year's presidential election.

events.title: ‘Call My Agent’ returns: George Clooney, Eva Longoria guest star in French film spinoff
events.summary: Manon Kerjean, FRANCE 24's film critic highlights some of her picks among the French films in competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. She also looks at new releases in French cinema: "15/18", a film set in a psychiatric unit which tackles mental health and "A Woman's Life" – a film starring Cesar-winning actress Léa Drucker as a woman whose organized life is upended by the arrival of a stranger. She also previews "The Unknown", a film by Arthur Hariri about two strangers who wake up in each other's bodies. Finally, she gives her thoughts on a highly anticipated film, "Call my Agent", which picks up five years after the end of the hit TV series on Netflix.

events.title: Pope merchandise flies off shelves as France gears up for pontiff's visit
events.summary: Tshirts, mugs and rosaries... These are just a few of the items available in the range of merchandise hitting souvenir shops ahead of Pope Leo XIV’s much anticipated visit to the northeastern French city of Metz on 28th September. The items have proved hugely popular, with some flying off the shelves quicker than shopkeepers can stock them.

events.title: Modern warfare: Ukraine racing to develop new interceptor drones
events.summary: In recent weeks, Russia has been deploying jet-powered Shahed-type drones against Ukraine, presenting a new challenge for Ukrainian air defences. Kyiv is now working to develop interceptor drones capable of matching their speed and bringing them down. FRANCE 24’s Gulliver Cragg is in Kielce, Poland, at one of Europe’s largest arms fairs. He is joined by Roman Hapachylo, CEO of DoD Solution, one of the companies developing these technologies.

events.title: 12 countries including France, UK and Canada to sanction Israeli settlements
events.summary: Twelve countries including Britain, Canada and France announced Tuesday they would sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, after increasing attacks by settlers against Palestinians in the occupied territory. Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, and Sweden also plan to issue restrictions on trade with the settlements, the nations' foreign ministers said in a joint statement. The action follows weeks of increasing attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the illegally occupied territory that has drawn widespread condemnation from the international community.

events.title: Putin and Trump discuss Ukraine in 'extremely frank' call
events.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and US counterpart Donald Trump on Tuesday discussed the Ukraine conflict in an "extremely frank" and constructive hour-long phone call, the Kremlin said. It came after US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Moscow and Kyiv over the weekend in an attempt to kickstart long-stalled US efforts to end the fighting. Washington has been pushing for fresh face-to-face talks between Moscow and Kyiv.

events.title: 'We need to put the tech bros back in their box,' says Baroness Beeban Kidron
events.summary: In this edition, one of the world’s leading campaigners against the increasing influence of Big Tech describes it as “generational injustice against children”. Baroness Beeban Kidron abandoned her thirty-year career as a world-renowned filmmaker, to challenge Big Tech, though she says it’s not necessarily the technology that is at fault, but the way we use it. In conversation with FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval, she talks about her book “Users – How big tech took control and How to Fight back”.

events.title: Suspected migrant smugglers go on trial in Paris over mass drowning in Channel
events.summary: Fourteen people went on trial in France on Tuesday over the death of at least 31 people in the Channel in 2021, the deadliest accident involving asylum seekers trying to reach the English coast. The trial carries particular significance because of the high death toll and the sheer number of civil parties involved, 114 in all, including victims' families. Some of them travelled from Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region to testify.

events.title: French Riviera heist: Renoir paintings stolen from French museum
events.summary: Police were on Tuesday hunting for two thieves who escaped with two Renoir paintings from a museum in southern France, after abandoning two others in its garden as they fled, a mayor said. The heist is the latest in a string of such robberies in France including the daylight theft last year of crown jewellery valued at around $100 million from the Louvre in Paris.

events.title: France’s record heatwave pushes champagne alcohol levels to historic high
events.summary: France’s record-breaking summer heat has forced champagne producers to contend with unusually high sugar levels in grapes, forcing authorities to allow alcohol content of up to 15 percent in the region’s sparkling wine for the first time. Champagne is usually capped at 13 percent.

events.title: The Times: 'Counterproductive' sanctions on Israel don't match the 'theatrical rhetoric'
events.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, September 9: British papers are reacting to the sanctions imposed on Israel. Next: Israeli papers discuss Haaretz's October 7 revelatory investigation. Also: CDs are back! Finally, South Park renames itself to South America to mock Trump.

events.title: Rungis market chief on supply chains and feeding the world
events.summary: In today’s edition, FRANCE 24’s Delano D'Souza speaks with the man at the heart of France's food supply chain. Stéphane Layani is the head of the Rungis wholesale food market – the largest of its kind in Europe – and chairman of the World Union of Wholesale Markets. Earlier this year Layani came out with a book titled Le Monde a faim, or "The World is Hungry" in English. In his interview, he gives his perspective on how France's food system will transform in the coming years.

events.title: The world's third global aerospace market: India's civil aviation sector takes off
events.summary: The aviation sector is one of the India's strongest-performing industries. More than 70 airports have been built over the past decade, and the country counts over 400 million air passengers annually. In just ten years, India has become the world's third-largest aviation market, behind China and the United States.

events.title: Serbia's Vucic calls snap elections after nearly two years of protests
events.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic on Wednesday called snap parliamentary elections for October 25. They are expected to be a key test of his right-wing populist Serbian Progressive Party after nearly two years of student-led anti-corruption protests.

events.title: Iran attacks US base after American strikes on tankers
events.summary: Iran said it fired ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan early Wednesday, in retaliation for US strikes on Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island, off Iran’s coast. The US said five Iranian tankers were destroyed.

events.title: 'New escalation in Yemen deeply concerning everyone in the region'
events.summary: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Jules Grange Gastinel, Researcher at the Institute for Research and Studies on the Arab and Muslim World (IREMAM). He depicts Yemen as moving from a prolonged condition of unresolved conflict into renewed regional confrontation. The relative calm established after 2022, he argues, never amounted to a durable political settlement: Yemen remains divided between rival political, financial and military institutions.

events.title: Houthis report Saudi reprisals after oil sites set ablaze in wave of strikes
events.summary: The Houthis said Saudi Arabia retaliated with strikes on Tuesday after the group targeted oil facilities, wounding dozens, as deadly fighting reignited in Yemen after a Houthi offensive towards the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab chokepoint. The rapid round of strikes and counter-strikes follows the unravelling of a four-year truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in July.

events.title: War in the Middle East: Iran attacks US base in Jordan, 10 US vessels
events.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they pummelled a US military base in Jordan, vowing retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers that dragged the foes deeper into war. Tehran's bombs came after US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to Iran targeting an American warship, the second such attack in less than a week. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran, Iran.

events.title: More than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans', insider warns

events.title: Prince of Wales joins mourners at funeral of Norway's King Harald

events.title: White House removes ‘Build the Wall’ game from website after Tetris posts warning
events.summary: The White House removed MAGA-themed game “Build the Wall” from its website this week after the Tetris Co.

events.title: Trump escalates Canada trade war, moving to ban imports of motorcycles, dairy and alcohol
events.summary: As the U.S.-Canadian relationship severely deteriorates, the White House says the import bans will go into effect in about three weeks.

events.title: As Trump pushes for data centers, voters in key midterm races say they don’t want them
events.summary: An NBC News Decision Desk Poll found that 69% of respondents oppose building AI data centers in their areas, with 45% saying they “strongly oppose” the idea.

events.title: Iran attacks American warships and base after U.S. sinks five Iranian tankers
events.summary: They’re the latest tit-for-tat strikes as Washington and Tehran lurch back toward fighting during more than six months of war.

events.title: Graphic: Tracking ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has been at a near-standstill for weeks amid the Iran war, sending prices of oil and other key goods soaring.

events.title: Oil hits $100 a barrel for first since July as Middle East conflict intensifies again
events.summary: The price of oil breached the $100 threshold Wednesday for the first time since July, as new flare-ups in the United States’ war with Iran stoked fresh concern for global energy markets.

events.title: Iran increases gasoline price for its heaviest consumers as economy struggles
events.summary: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran early Tuesday introduced a higher price for its heaviest users of gasoline, state media reported, in the latest economic pinch caused by months of war.

events.title: Bayeux Tapestry on display in London after nearly 1,000 years
events.summary: A priceless art piece has left France to go on display temporarily in England after nearly 1,000 years. The Bayeux Tapestry is a 230-foot-long piece of ancient art that depicts the Battle of Hastings in 1066. NBC News' Daniele Hamamdjian previews the exhibit that has been sold out for months.

events.title: New Russian attacks on Ukraine
events.summary: NBC News’ Richard Engel is on the ground in Kyiv and reports from the scene of a bloody new strike by Russia. Attacks resumed after a brief three day pause as President Trump’s envoys were in the region trying to relaunch peace efforts.

events.title: Tech company discloses first-of-its-kind A.I. cyberattack of one government against another
events.summary: Israeli cyber security firm Dream says it disclosed an A.I. hack working to compromise a government entity in Asia, thousands of miles away. NBC News’ Keir Simmons reports.

events.title: Prince George starts his first day at elite Eton College
events.summary: 13-year-old Prince George started his first day at one of Britain's most elite schools, Eton College. The future British king followed in the footsteps of Prince William and Prince Harry, who also attended Eton.

events.title: China hits back at U.S. claim its AI companies systematically copied American models
events.summary: In its most detailed accusation yet, the U.S. government has named six Chinese AI companies that it says copied American companies for their AI secrets.

events.title: Widespread flight delays hit major British airports
events.summary: Flights departing from two of London’s Heathrow Airport have been grounded following a “technical issue.”

events.title: Chinese hackers are running AI on stolen networks to avoid detection, Google says
events.summary: One China-linked group targets academic, medical and military AI research, the report says.

events.title: Harry and Meghan ‘surprised’ by king’s letter making clear they’re still nonworking royals
events.summary: A spokesman for the couple told NBC News that a government committee was meeting this week to discuss whether to provide security for the family now that they have moved back to the U.K.

events.title: King Charles confirms Harry and Meghan will not be working royals after U.K. return
events.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan will not be working members of Britain’s royal family now they have returned to the U.K., a letter sent on behalf of King Charles said.

events.title: U.S. envoys ‘very encouraged’ after peace talks in Moscow and Kyiv
events.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner said talks were “substantive,” but neither gave details of any proposal to end the conflict.

events.title: U.S. strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets Navy warships, military says
events.summary: U.S. Central Command said no American personnel were harmed in the Iranian missile attacks.

events.title: Serbia accused of ‘glorifying’ convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić ahead of funeral
events.summary: BELGRADE, Serbia — The European Union’s Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos on Friday canceled an upcoming visit to candidate nation Serbia over what she described as the “glorification” of former Bosnian Serb army commander Ratko Mladić following his death.

events.title: Two trapped workers pulled alive from Nepal tunnel more than a week after deadly floods
events.summary: Two workers in Nepal were pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel on Friday, some nine days after devastating floods swept the Himalayan region and left thousands of people missing.

events.title: Senior aides to British Trump ally Nigel Farage step down after foreign funding sting
events.summary: Britain’s populist Reform UK said two senior aides to leader Nigel Farage stepped down on Friday after an undercover investigation alleged the party had broken electoral law by arranging for a foreign donor to pay for political polling.

events.title: In Nepal, mourners hold symbolic cremation for missing loved ones
events.summary: As hopes for those still missing fade, families without the remains of their relatives are burning effigies on miniature funeral pyres.
